subproblem.title: Approximate tangent spaces glue over a countable Borel cover of a locally Hⁿ-finite set, given tangent locality (TL) (parent Step 6; Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2))
subproblem.statement:
Assume (TL): for all P, n ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and all Borel sets A ⊆ B ⊆ U with Hⁿ(B ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), the following holds for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A and every linear subspace Q of ℝ^P: B has approximate tangent space Q at x iff A does (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt, Simon Ch. 3, 1.4).
Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and B ⊆ U Borel with Hⁿ(B ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U. Let S_j (j ∈ ℕ) be Borel sets with S_j ⊆ B for every j and B ⊆ ⋃_j S_j. Let Q assign to each x ∈ ℝ^P a linear subspace Q(x) of ℝ^P. Suppose that for every j, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ S_j, S_j has approximate tangent space Q(x) at x. Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ B, B has approximate tangent space Q(x) at x.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U A B : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet B → A ⊆ B → B ⊆ U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (B ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict A), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q) → ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U B : Set (Euclid P)) (S : ℕ → Set (Euclid P)) (Q : Euclid P → Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet B → B ⊆ U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (B ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → (∀ j, MeasurableSet (S j)) → (∀ j, S j ⊆ B) → B ⊆ ⋃ j, S j → (∀ j, ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict (S j)), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (S j) x (Q x)) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict B), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x (Q x)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent Step 6, which transfers approximate tangent spaces from the piece slices S^j_t to M_t via (TL) and then takes a countable union of null sets. This is the mechanism behind Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2): T_xM = T_xN_j for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_j (chapter-03.txt ll. 86–90), with the decomposition of Remark 1.3 (ll. 67–72). It is used in Ch. 6, proof of Lemma 4.1(2) (chapter-06.txt ll. 1173–1181).

Notation: Hⁿ = μHE[n]. Let E := {x ∈ ℝ^P : B does not have approximate tangent space Q(x) at x}. We must show Hⁿ⌞B(E) = 0. Since B is Borel, this is Hⁿ(E ∩ B) = 0.

1. Locality on one piece. Fix j. Apply (TL) with (P, n, U, A, B) := (P, n, U, S_j, B). Its hypotheses hold:
 - U is open;
 - S_j and B are Borel;
 - S_j ⊆ B ⊆ U;
 - Hⁿ(B ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U.
 Hence there is an Hⁿ⌞S_j-null set N¹_j such that for every x ∉ N¹_j and every linear subspace Q' of ℝ^P: B has approximate tangent space Q' at x iff S_j does.

2. Transfer on one piece.
 - By hypothesis there is an Hⁿ⌞S_j-null set N²_j such that for x ∉ N²_j, S_j has approximate tangent space Q(x) at x.
 - For x ∉ N¹_j ∪ N²_j, which is again Hⁿ⌞S_j-null, step 1 with Q' := Q(x) shows that B has approximate tangent space Q(x) at x.
 - Therefore Hⁿ⌞S_j(E) = 0.
 - Since S_j is Borel, Hⁿ⌞S_j(E) = Hⁿ(E ∩ S_j) for the arbitrary set E (Measure.restrict_apply'). So Hⁿ(E ∩ S_j) = 0.

3. Countable union. By countable subadditivity, Hⁿ(E ∩ ⋃_j S_j) ≤ Σ_j Hⁿ(E ∩ S_j) = 0. In Lean: a property holds Hⁿ⌞(⋃_j S_j)-a.e. iff it holds Hⁿ⌞S_j-a.e. for every j (ae_restrict_iUnion_iff). So B has approximate tangent space Q(x) at x for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ ⋃_j S_j.

4. Restriction to B. Since B ⊆ ⋃_j S_j, monotonicity gives Hⁿ(E ∩ B) ≤ Hⁿ(E ∩ ⋃_j S_j) = 0 (in Lean: ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset). Hence for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ B, B has approximate tangent space Q(x) at x. ∎
proof_key_steps: Apply (TL) with (A, B) := (S_j, B) (S_j, B Borel, S_j ⊆ B ⊆ U, B locally Hⁿ-finite): for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ S_j, B and S_j have the same approximate tangent spaces at x.
Combine with the piece hypothesis: for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ S_j, B has approximate tangent space Q(x) at x.
A countable union of null sets is null, so the property holds Hⁿ-a.e. on ⋃_j S_j (ae_restrict_iUnion_iff).
B ⊆ ⋃_j S_j gives the property Hⁿ-a.e. on B (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset).

audit.reason: All TL, Borel, containment and local-finiteness hypotheses match. TL is applied in the correct direction on each piece and evaluated at Q(x); no measurability of Q is needed. Countable a.e. gluing and restriction to B complete the exact conclusion. The parent's compact-piece argument supplies the premises needed for G4b.
